name: sender-naming
description: How the phone names a conversation/sender for replicas such as GMweb. The phone sends identity and provenance; the replica owns user overrides and the shared directory.

address.description: Raw provider sender, byte for byte. This is the identity; never normalize or replace it for display.

senderKind.description: How the address must be interpreted. A short code or alphanumeric sender is not a subscriber number.

displayName.description: A human name when source is CONTACT; otherwise the address itself. Never blank.

displayNameSource.description: Provenance of displayName. ADDRESS means 'fallback, not a human name'; a consumer MUST NOT replace a USER, CONTACT or DIRECTORY name with it.

rules: address is always the raw provider sender and is always present in conversation and message payloads (it may be empty only when the provider truly supplied nothing).
displayName is never an empty string. When no contact name exists, the producer sets displayName = address and displayNameSource = ADDRESS.
displayNameSource = ADDRESS is a fallback. A consumer must not overwrite a USER, CONTACT or DIRECTORY name with it; that is what turned a known bank name into 'Unknown conversation'.
When displayNameSource = ADDRESS the consumer must render the address (or a directory name), never the literal label 'Unknown conversation'.
USER is the operator's rename and has the highest precedence. DIRECTORY is a shared/curated sender directory (bank/service short codes); the phone does not ship one.
A consumer may add its own USER/DIRECTORY names but must keep the producer's address and senderKind untouched.
Consumers must not infer a bank name from message body text; that requires the shared directory, not guessing.

examples.note: A long numeric bank sender id. A directory may name it; without one, render the address, not 'Unknown conversation'.
